# GitHub profile achievements

[Türkçe](ACHIEVEMENTS.tr.md)

## Earnable

### Tiered

#### Pull Shark

**How to earn:** Open pull requests that get merged. PRs in your own repositories count too.

**Tiers:** 2 · x2: 16 · x3: 128 · x4: 1024

**Tip:** Look for small fixes in projects you already use: broken links, outdated docs, typos in examples, issues labeled "good first issue".

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### Starstruck

**How to earn:** Create a repository that reaches the star count. It has to be a single repo you own, forks don't count.

**Tiers:** 16 · x2: 128 · x3: 512 · x4: 4096

**Tip:** A clear README with a screenshot or GIF, a license and a one-line install command go a long way. Then share it where your audience actually is.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### Galaxy Brain

**How to earn:** Answer questions in GitHub Discussions and get your answers marked as accepted.

**Tiers:** 2 · x2: 8 · x3: 16 · x4: 32

**Tip:** Answers in github.com/orgs/community don't count since February 2024. Pick repos where maintainers actually mark answers, and back your answer with docs or source links.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### Pair Extraordinaire

**How to earn:** Be a co-author on a commit in a merged pull request.

**Tiers:** 1 · x2: 10 · x3: 24 · x4: 48

**Tip:** The easiest real way: leave a suggestion in someone's PR review. When they click "Commit suggestion", GitHub adds you as co-author. The email in a Co-authored-by line has to be linked to your account.

**Tracked by this tool:** no

### One-time

#### Quickdraw

**How to earn:** Close an issue or a pull request within 5 minutes of opening it.

**Tip:** Happens naturally when you open an issue and immediately fix it with a PR that says "Closes #N".

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### YOLO

**How to earn:** Merge a pull request without a code review.

**Tip:** Any PR you merge yourself in a repo without required reviews does it.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### Public Sponsor

**How to earn:** Sponsor someone through GitHub Sponsors with your sponsorship visible to everyone.

**Tip:** A one-time sponsorship works too. Many maintainers accept a custom amount, so it doesn't have to be expensive. Keep "Who can see your sponsorship?" on Everyone.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

### Profile highlights

#### PRO

**How to earn:** Use a GitHub Pro plan.

**Tip:** Students get Pro for free through the GitHub Student Developer Pack (education.github.com/pack). Graduate students count too.

**Tracked by this tool:** no

#### Developer Program Member

**How to earn:** Register for the GitHub Developer Program while building something that uses the GitHub API.

**Tip:** Register at github.com/developer/register with a support email and a website for your integration.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### Security advisory credit

**How to earn:** Get a contribution to the GitHub Advisory Database accepted.

**Tip:** You don't need to find a new vulnerability. Improving an existing advisory (missing CWE, affected versions, fix commit) through "Suggest improvements" or a PR to github/advisory-database counts.

**Tracked by this tool:** no

#### Security Bug Bounty Hunter

**How to earn:** Report a valid vulnerability to the GitHub Security Bug Bounty program.

**Tip:** Scope and rules are at bounty.github.com. The GitHub mobile apps are in scope too.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### GitHub Campus Expert

**How to earn:** Take part in the GitHub Campus Expert program as a student community leader.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

#### GitHub Star

**How to earn:** Get nominated and selected for the GitHub Stars program, which recognizes people who share knowledge with the community.

**Tip:** Talks, blog posts, videos and podcasts about open source are what the program looks for. Nominations are at stars.github.com.

**Tracked by this tool:** yes

- **Mars 2020 Contributor:** Given to contributors of the open source projects used in the Mars 2020 helicopter mission. Can't be earned anymore.

## FAQ

**I did the thing but the badge isn't showing.**

It can take a few minutes, sometimes longer. Also check Settings > Public profile > Contributions & activity: achievements can be hidden there, and private contributions only count when "Include private contributions on my profile" is on.

**My commits don't count.**

The commit email has to be added and verified on your GitHub account. Check it with `git log --format='%ae'` and compare it with github.com/settings/emails.

**Can I farm badges with a second account?**

GitHub's terms allow one free personal account per person, so a second account just for badges breaks the rules. You don't need it anyway: every badge here can be earned with real work.

**Where do these rules come from?**

GitHub doesn't publish the exact criteria. The thresholds come from what the community has observed, mainly the list at github.com/Schweinepriester/github-profile-achievements. If something changes, please open an issue.
